findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification when a totpCode is also sent
findings.body: Password verification is gated on `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` (line 121), while the backup-code branch is entered whenever `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is truthy (line 131), regardless of whether a `totpCode` was supplied. Because these two conditions are independent, a request that contains a valid backup code AND any non-empty `totpCode` value skips password checking but still goes through the backup-code validation path. The consequence is that anyone holding a single leaked backup code can log in with just that code plus a garbage totpCode, without knowing the account password — the backup code ceases to be a second factor and becomes a single factor. The UI happens to set `totpCode` to an empty string in backup mode, so this is only reachable by calling the credentials provider directly, but it is a real authentication bypass of the password requirement. The backup-code branch should also require the password (or the password check should not be skipped merely because `totpCode` is present when `backupCode` is being used).

findings.title: Backup code single-use enforcement is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: Backup-code consumption is implemented as: decrypt the stored array, set `backupCodes[index] = null`, then `prisma.user.update` with a re-encrypted copy. This is a classic TOCTOU read-modify-write with no locking or conditional update. Two concurrent login requests that present the same backup code can both read the pre-update value, both find the code valid, and both succeed — so a single backup code can be used more than once under concurrency. Since backup codes are a recovery/second-factor credential, being able to replay one defeats the 'used exactly once' guarantee stated in the UI copy. A conditional/atomic update (e.g. compare-and-set on the ciphertext, or a DB transaction with row lock) is needed.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog after enabling 2FA never calls onEnable, leaving the toggle out of sync
findings.body: Previously `handleEnable` called `onEnable()` immediately on success. Now it transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, and `onEnable()` is only invoked from the explicit 'Close' button (line 269). The `Dialog`'s `onOpenChange` (line 166) is still wired straight to the parent, so a user who dismisses the modal via Escape, backdrop click, or the close (X) button after the TOTP code was accepted leaves the server-side 2FA enabled (the enable endpoint already set `twoFactorEnabled: true`) while the parent never runs `onEnable()` / refetch, so the settings switch and related state can continue to display 2FA as disabled. The finalization should happen on any close path (or the parent should refetch on close), not only on the dedicated Close button.

findings.title: No test covers the core feature: logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The PR description's checklist explicitly states no tests were added, and the added e2e steps only click the download and copy buttons and then close the dialog; both content assertions are left as `// TODO` and nothing exercises the actual backup-code path. The two security-sensitive behaviors this PR introduces — consuming a backup code during login (single-use invalidation) and disabling 2FA via a backup code — have zero automated coverage. Given the password-bypass and single-use race described elsewhere, the absence of a test that actually signs in with a backup code and asserts that the same code is then rejected leaves these regressions undetected. At minimum, a login-with-backup-code test (and the already-flagged 'TODO' file-content check) should be added.

findings.title: Existing 2FA users have no backup codes and no way to generate them, making 'Lost access' a dead end
findings.body: `backupCodes` is a new nullable column, so every user who enabled 2FA before this migration has `user.backupCodes === null`. When such a user uses 'Lost access' and submits anything, they hit `if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes)`, which renders `t("missing_backup_codes")` = 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' That instruction is impossible to follow: the only endpoint that creates backup codes is `setup.ts`, which returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` for users who already have 2FA on, and this PR adds no 'regenerate backup codes' UI. These users are therefore permanently locked out of the recovery path (they must disable and re-enable 2FA, which is exactly what the feature is meant to avoid). Either the message should not tell users to do something the product does not offer, or a way to generate/regenerate backup codes for already-enabled 2FA should be provided.

findings.title: Exhausting all backup codes reports 'incorrect code' instead of 'no backup codes'
findings.body: After codes are consumed they are set to `null` but the array (and therefore the encrypted string) is never emptied, so `user.backupCodes` remains a truthy JSON string of nulls. The guard on line 137 (`if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes)`) never fires once all codes are used; instead `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` returns -1 and the user is told `incorrect_backup_code` forever. A user with zero remaining codes should be told they have none left (the `MissingBackupCodes` path) rather than being told each retry that their code is wrong.
